latest_news.headline: Reuters reports October 9 Putin-Trump call: immediate Ukraine peace talks deemed unlikely
latest_news.text: Reuters reporting published by Al Jazeera on October 10 at 01:40:51 UTC describes a Putin-Trump telephone call on Friday, October 9. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov says Putin regards an immediate resumption of trilateral Ukraine peace talks as unlikely, citing drone attacks during the previous month’s parliamentary elections. This is an attributed statement about negotiations, not independent verification of the drone claims, termination of all diplomacy or a new attack. Reuters also reports Trump announced a Russian diesel-supply agreement after the call and that Ukraine and European allies criticised it. The complete Reuters article was read; the underlying Kremlin transcript and an independent account of the conversation were not retrieved. The exact call instant and a confirmed next negotiating date remain unknown. No nuclear-alert, military-escalation or urgent qualification is established.
latest_news.originating_source: Reuters original reporting carried by Al Jazeera, quoting Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov
latest_news.implication: The Kremlin account casts doubt on immediate trilateral talks; it does not establish that all diplomacy has ended or that military escalation has occurred.
latest_news.next_trigger: No confirmed date for resumed trilateral talks is supplied.

latest_news.headline: Lebanon: six wounded reported near Hawsh al-Sayyed Ali; target identity unverified
latest_news.text: Newly reviewed October 9 reporting describes a strike near a vehicle at Hawsh al-Sayyed Ali in Lebanon's Hermel district near the Syrian border. Asharq Al-Awsat quotes Lebanon's health ministry reporting six wounded: five Syrian nationals, including two women, and one Lebanese. It also attributes an Israeli military statement identifying the alleged target as Yusuf Ali al-Hassoun and alleging Iranian direction; neither identity, role nor a target death is authenticated here. Anadolu says witnesses told its reporters the missile landed beside, not directly on, the vehicle and quotes medical sources for six minor injuries. L'Orient's correspondent similarly reports six minor injuries and describes video showing a vehicle beside a crater; the original video was not authenticated, and whether the injured were in the vehicle is unclear. Original health-ministry, NNA and Israeli military statements were not retrieved. These reports are distinct from the retained Zawtar tree-clearing episode. Exact event, publication and verification instants remain unknown. Different news hosts and anonymous accounts do not establish independent verification; no urgent qualification is claimed.
latest_news.originating_source: Asharq Al-Awsat attributed official accounts; original Anadolu and L’Orient witness/correspondent reporting
latest_news.implication: Six injuries are reported near the Syrian border; casualty details and the alleged target identity are not independently verified.
latest_news.next_trigger: No follow-up timetable or independently evidenced next operational trigger is supplied.

latest_news.headline: Newly reviewed IAEA Update 370: limited inspection finds damage near reported October 5 drone incident
latest_news.text: The original October 9 IAEA Update 370 incident and inspection paragraphs were read through direct publication extraction. The agency says its Zaporizhzhya team was informed of a reported drone attack on a laboratory and utility building and a radioactive-waste-processing building between midnight and 00:30 local time on October 5. It reports no casualties or radiation leaks for that building incident. Local time is retained without an assumed UTC offset. After requesting access, the team received limited access more than 48 hours later. It observed broken windows, piles of glass, covered openings and an approximately 40-centimetre pavement-damage area; UAV components were displayed at the site. The team concludes buildings near the reported incident sustained physical damage, but the statement does not independently establish the cause or responsible actor. Separately, the plant told the agency on October 5 that a delivery driver had been killed in a reported attack the previous day; this is a separate attributed account, not a casualty in the building incident. Grossi calls for prompt, unfettered access to reported attack sites and identifies continuing nuclear-safety risks. This is newly reviewed October 5 reporting, not a new October 9 attack. Exact publication and inspection instants are unknown. No independent two-source confirmation, radiation emergency or urgent qualification is claimed.
latest_news.originating_source: IAEA original Update 370, limited inspection observations and plant-attributed incident accounts
latest_news.implication: The IAEA observed physical damage near the reported October 5 incident after limited access; cause, responsibility and the separate driver-death account remain unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: The IAEA calls for prompt, unfettered access to reported attack sites; no findings timetable is supplied.

latest_news.headline: L'Orient reports tree clearing near Lebanese Army position in Zawtar Gharbieh
latest_news.text: L'Orient Today's original October 9 article, including additional reporting by Muntasser Abdallah, was read through publication extraction. It reports an Israeli force with a military bulldozer continuing tree clearing Friday near Zawtar Gharbieh's water reservoir, about 50 metres from a Lebanese Army position. It says tree clearing began Thursday and that Lebanese forces deployed in the village in July under the framework agreement. This specifically located correspondent account is distinct from the retained October 7 UNIFIL Kfar Shouba gunfire report. The article also describes other artillery and airstrike reporting, but no independently established Israeli-Lebanese clash, casualties at this location or new strategic deployment is inferred. Anadolu's separate article attributes broader shelling to Lebanon's National News Agency and does not independently confirm this tree-clearing incident. Exact event and publication instants, underlying visual authentication and independent verification are unknown. The displayed 13:05 publication clock has no observed UTC offset and is not converted.
latest_news.originating_source: L'Orient Today original correspondent reporting, including Muntasser Abdallah
latest_news.implication: The report places tree clearing close to a Lebanese Army post; no clash, casualty or independent confirmation is established.
latest_news.next_trigger: No follow-up timetable or independently evidenced next operational trigger is supplied by the report.

latest_news.headline: Zaporizhzhia revision: administration raises October 9 injury tally to 23; scope not fully reconciled
latest_news.text: The original Zaporizhzhia regional administration Telegram post 68238, published October 9 at 17:06:15 UTC, raises the number of people injured by attacks over the course of the day to 23 and says medical assistance is being provided. Its quoted earlier post describes six guided aerial bombs at dawn, one man killed and 16 injured including a 14-year-old child. Ukrinform at 21:37 local time reports 23 injuries and one death in its account of the morning city attack; its quoted official update explicitly covers attacks over the day. This supersedes the earlier five- and seven-injury evidence account for the retained October 9 reporting group without treating the entire daily count as independently confirmed casualties in one strike. Exact geographic and incident scope of the expanded count is not fully reconciled. Medical records and independent casualty verification were not retrieved. This is a later casualty-account revision concerning October 9, not a new October 10 attack. Ukrinform says recovery work continues Saturday.
latest_news.originating_source: Zaporizhzhia regional administration original Telegram post; Ukrinform relays official casualty account
latest_news.implication: The official injury account has risen to 23 across the day; its exact attack scope and casualty total are not independently verified.
latest_news.next_trigger: Ukrinform says recovery work continues Saturday; no casualty-reconciliation timetable is supplied.

latest_news.headline: Newly reviewed October 9 advisory: Saudi airspace risk recommendations expanded
latest_news.text: The original CZIB-2026-09-R1 was read in full from EASA's public page. It displays an initial issue date of September 30, an October 9 revision date and validity through November 16 unless reviewed earlier. The revision description says its description and recommendations were revised to reflect a changed risk area. It describes repeated attacks affecting Riyadh and aviation infrastructure, including risks to aircraft on the ground and during take-off and landing, misidentification, interception activity and falling debris. For its specified EASA and TCO applicability, it recommends not operating at any altitude within portions of Saudi airspace defined by the Jeddah FIR boundary and the lines RIBOK - BOSUT - MIGDA - RAGNO - MIXUG - DEKLO - OBSAM - SILPA, and ULBAM - TOTEB - DURMA - LAKSO - SOLAT; it recommends caution elsewhere in Jeddah FIR, up-to-date risk assessment and contingency planning. This is a revised public safety advisory, not a verified new attack, blanket closure of Saudi airspace or an operating approval. Exact publication/revision instant is not supplied. The original full recommendations, not AP's shorter summary, control the account.
latest_news.originating_source: EASA original Conflict Zone Information Bulletin
latest_news.implication: The revised advisory highlights greater aviation-infrastructure exposure and defined no-operation areas; it is not a blanket Saudi airspace closure.
latest_news.next_trigger: The bulletin is valid until November 16 unless reviewed earlier; it calls for close monitoring of aeronautical publications and short-notice instructions.

latest_news.headline: UKMTO Warning 160-26: projectile strike and extinguished fire reported west of Al Jazeera, UAE
latest_news.text: UKMTO's original Warning 160-26, marked ATTACK and Source Third Party, gives the incident date as October 9 and time as 1000 UTC. It says it received multiple-source reports that an unnamed vessel 13 nautical miles west of Al Jazeera, UAE, was struck by an unknown projectile, causing a fire that was subsequently extinguished. Crew status, damage and environmental impact are explicitly unknown, and authorities are investigating. The original PDF text was read in full; direct bytes could not be retrieved. gCaptain and Anadolu repeat this same notice and are not independent verification. The notice does not identify the vessel, responsible actor or weapon. The separately reviewed IRGC NV Sunshine claim is not linked to this numbered warning. No injury, death, pollution, closure or attribution is inferred.
latest_news.originating_source: UKMTO original Warning 160-26, third-party reporting
latest_news.implication: The notice reports a vessel fire inside the Gulf; crew condition, damage, environmental impact and responsibility remain unknown.
latest_news.next_trigger: UKMTO says authorities are investigating and advises cautious transit and reporting suspicious activity; no findings timetable is supplied.

latest_news.headline: Riyadh airport revision: AP reports foreign-carrier suspensions despite resumed operations
latest_news.text: AP's October 9 report, published by Fortune at 14:00:20 UTC and read in its original HTML, reports at least 124 Riyadh flights cancelled by Friday afternoon according to FlightAware. It attributes Air India's suspension through Saturday to the Indian Embassy, Lufthansa Group's suspension through October 16 to the group, and Pakistan International Airlines' suspension to an airline spokesman. These reported foreign-carrier restrictions qualify the retained GACA/Saudia resumption accounts; they do not prove the airport is closed or that all traffic stopped. Original airline/embassy notices and the underlying FlightAware data were not recovered. The publication repeats three GACA-attributed deaths and Saudia's pilot/aircraft account for the retained October 8 episode; no new casualty total or October 9 attack is added. Exact suspension start/end UTC instants and present flight availability remain unknown. The independent EASA advisory is retained as a separate documentary report, not verification of this casualty count.
latest_news.originating_source: Associated Press reporting by Cara Anna and Sally Abou Aljoud, syndicated by Fortune
latest_news.implication: Reported foreign-carrier suspensions persist despite GACA/Saudia resumption accounts; actual flight availability and the reported cancellation count remain unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: AP reports Air India suspended through Saturday and Lufthansa Group through October 16; exact resumption times are not supplied.
latest_news.material_revision: AP adds reported foreign-carrier suspensions and Friday cancellations; Saudia resumption does not establish all airlines resumed.

latest_news.headline: Adigrat revision: Reuters reports Ethiopia's UN letter alleges invasion and invokes self-defence
latest_news.text: Reuters' October 9 report, read in full on CNBC Africa, describes a letter dated October 8 from Ethiopian Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos to French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot. A senior Ethiopian official shared it with Reuters and said it was also sent to other UN Security Council members. The letter alleges an all-out Eritrean invasion and advances of up to 60 km into Tigray, and invokes Ethiopia's right to self-defence. This adds an attributed government position to the retained Adigrat deployment and strike episode; it does not independently establish an invasion or a separate combat event. Reuters says Eritrea's information minister had disputed incursion reports on October 7 and did not immediately respond on October 9. Reuters also attributes October 7-8 drone strikes to ACLED and reports an Adigrat resident hearing explosions overnight and into October 9. The original Ethiopian letter, the minister's original denial, the ACLED briefing, troop nationality and strike attribution were not independently authenticated. CNBC Africa and Internazionale carry the same Reuters report, not independent confirmation. Exact letter dispatch, crossing and strike times are unknown. No further operational trigger or follow-up timetable is supplied.
latest_news.originating_source: Reuters reporting carried by CNBC Africa and Internazionale; Ethiopian letter attributed, original not recovered
latest_news.implication: Reuters reports a formal Ethiopian self-defence claim over the retained border episode; invasion, troop identity and strike attribution remain unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: No independently evidenced next operational trigger or follow-up timetable is supplied.
latest_news.material_revision: Reuters adds the Ethiopian government letter alleging incursion and invoking self-defence to the same retained border episode.

latest_news.headline: Adigrat revision: updated Reuters dispatch adds Eritrea's counter-accusation
latest_news.text: The October 9 Reuters dispatch, read in full in CNBC Africa's original HTML, now includes Eritrean Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel's response, attributed to a Friday statement on X. He says Ethiopia has pursued an unprovoked war of aggression for more than three years, links this to Ethiopia's stated sea-access ambitions and accuses it of seeking Assab. Reuters says the new statement did not address Eritrean troops deploying in Ethiopia and recalls the minister's October 7 rejection of incursion reports. The original Ethiopian letter dated October 8 and the original Eritrean X statement were not recovered. This revises the retained response-pending account of the same Adigrat deployment episode; it does not establish a separate invasion, a new declaration of war or independently verified troop identity, responsibility or damage. The same dispatch adds Ethiopian Airlines' attributed plan to resume Mekelle flights on October 11; the original airline notice was not retrieved, so no completed reopening or territorial-control claim is made. Original HTML structured metadata preserves publication at 09:19:24 UTC and modification at 16:03:19 UTC October 9. Reuters syndication is not independent confirmation.
latest_news.originating_source: Reuters dispatch carried by CNBC Africa; Ethiopian letter and Eritrean minister's X statement attributed
latest_news.implication: Updated Reuters reporting adds Eritrea's counter-accusation to the same border episode; neither invasion nor troop identity is independently verified.
latest_news.next_trigger: No independently evidenced next operational trigger or follow-up timetable is supplied.
latest_news.material_revision: Updated dispatch adds Eritrea's counter-accusation to the same episode, replacing the earlier response-pending account.

latest_news.headline: Riyadh airport revision: GACA reports three killed; Saudia reports operations resumed
latest_news.text: AP's October 9 report attributes to Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation three Saudi citizens killed and several people injured in two October 8 attacks targeting Riyadh airport facilities and a Saudia aircraft. Gulf News and Sabq likewise report that statement. This is newly reviewed fatal-casualty reporting for the retained October 8 airport episode, not a new October 9 attack; the earlier three deaths at Riyadh and Abha on October 6-7 are a different account and are not reassigned here. Reuters separately reports Saudia's statement that one employee died, one aircraft was damaged on the ground, no passengers were aboard and the airline's flights and operations had returned to normal as of 6 p.m. Thursday. The employee count is not added to GACA's three: overlap is unresolved. The original GACA and Saudia statements were not directly retrieved, and reporting hosts repeating these official accounts do not independently confirm the casualties, responsible actor, damage extent or present flight availability. The exact event instants, original-statement publication times and reopening UTC instant remain unknown. Retained Reuters one-plane and AFP three-plane damage accounts remain unchanged; this review does not resolve that count. GACA is reported to be assessing damage; no findings timetable is supplied. Saudia's operational claim does not establish that all foreign airlines resumed service.
latest_news.originating_source: Reuters original reporting syndicated by Devdiscourse; AP original report; GACA and Saudia statements as reported
latest_news.implication: Official accounts now report fatal casualties in the retained October 8 episode and resumed airline operations; casualty totals and current flight availability remain unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: GACA is reported to be assessing damage; no findings timetable or independently evidenced further operational trigger is supplied.
latest_news.material_revision: Adds GACA-attributed fatal casualties for October 8 and Saudia-attributed employee death and resumed operations; physical consequences not independently verified.

latest_news.headline: Newly reviewed October 9 Zaporizhzhia attack: one death reported; injury accounts differ
latest_news.text: RBC-Ukraine's October 9 report was read in full. It retains the earlier administration account of one man killed and five people injured in six morning strikes, then attributes a later seven-injury count to the Zaporizhzhia Regional Defense Council. The original council update was not retrieved; the timing of that count and whether its scope exactly matches the earlier five-injury account are unknown. Retain the original administration report and present seven as a later attributed report, not a independently confirmed total. This is an evidence-account revision for the same October 9 attack reporting group, not a new attack. Do not combine October 8 Telegram injury updates, or the separate Ivano-Frankivsk and Bucha casualties in AP's national roundup, with this city incident. The exact event instant and independent casualty verification remain unknown.
latest_news.originating_source: RBC-Ukraine original article relaying regional administration and Defense Council casualty accounts
latest_news.implication: One death is officially reported; a later report attributes seven injuries to the regional council, but the casualty scope is not independently verified.
latest_news.next_trigger: No independently evidenced casualty-reconciliation timetable or next operational trigger is supplied.

latest_news.headline: Zaporizhzhia administration reports one killed and five injured in October 9 residential-area strikes
latest_news.text: The original Zaporizhzhia regional administration Telegram post 68208, published October 9 at 03:40:03 UTC, says Russian forces carried out six strikes on Zaporizhzhia that morning, killing one man and wounding five people including a child. It describes residential-area damage and a strike near an extracurricular education facility, with emergency services assisting casualties. Earlier post 68207 corrects the location from a residential building to near a high-rise building. AP reporting through ABC and Ukrinform repeat the official one-death/five-injury account. These are attributed official claims, not independently verified casualty or weapons assessments. This October 9 city attack is separate from the retained October 6 bridge strike and nuclear-site reports. Exact attack time is unknown. No independent verification or urgent qualification is claimed.
latest_news.originating_source: Zaporizhzhia regional administration original Telegram account; AP and Ukrinform relay official casualty reports
latest_news.implication: The administration reports civilian casualties and residential-area damage; casualty details and responsibility remain attributed official accounts.
latest_news.next_trigger: Emergency services are responding; no independently evidenced follow-up timetable is supplied.

latest_news.headline: Newly reviewed October 8 release: Saudi Civil Defence reports debris damages Riyadh kindergarten and clinic
latest_news.text: Saudi Press Agency Arabic release N2696566 quotes the Civil Defence spokesman saying that on Thursday October 8 in Riyadh, fragments from a ballistic missile after interception and destruction caused material damage at a kindergarten and a medical clinic complex. The spokesman attributes the missile to the Houthis and says approved response procedures were carried out. The full original body was read in the browser and retained in original HTML metadata and structured data. AP and AFP reporting repeat the same Civil Defence statement, not independent physical verification. Reuters describes these locations separately from the airport plane fire. No casualty figure, damage extent, exact event time, independent attribution, follow-up timetable or further operational trigger is supplied. The displayed publication clock is 16:32 without a UTC offset established in this review; it is not converted. This is a newly reviewed October 8 report, not a new attack today.
latest_news.originating_source: Saudi Civil Defence spokesman original announcement via Saudi Press Agency
latest_news.implication: Civil Defence reports civilian-site damage from interception debris, separately from the airport; casualties, damage extent and attribution remain unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: No follow-up timetable or independently evidenced next operational trigger is supplied by the statement.

latest_news.headline: Riyadh airport revision: AFP source reports three damaged planes; count and cause unverified
latest_news.text: AFP reporting published October 9 and read in full says two witnesses described cracks and holes in a Saudia aircraft fuselage, while a source briefed on the matter said three planes suffered damage at Riyadh airport. The article explicitly places the explosions and reported damage on October 8. This expands the retained Reuters account of one heavily damaged parked plane, but the aircraft count, identities of additional planes, damage severity, cause and any injuries remain unverified. The anonymous source overlap with Reuters and AP is unknown. It is a same-incident evidence revision, not a new October 9 attack or proof that a Houthi missile hit the aircraft. Previous airport deaths described by the article belong to earlier attacks and are not assigned to this event.
latest_news.originating_source: AFP original reporting syndicated by Malay Mail
latest_news.implication: Expanded damage reporting concerns the retained October 8 airport episode, not a new attack today; aircraft count, cause and injuries remain unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: The airport advises checking flights with airlines; no damage-assessment, reopening or investigation timetable is supplied.
latest_news.material_revision: AFP now reports a source claim of three damaged planes, extending retained one-plane reporting; count, cause and injuries unverified.

latest_news.headline: Newly reviewed UKMTO 159-26: October 6 tanker strike in Hormuz; damage unknown
latest_news.text: UKMTO Warning 159-26 is a time-late report of a crude-oil tanker struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on October 6 at 17:09 UTC. The original notice says no casualties have been reported; damage assessment and environmental impact are unknown. UKMTO says authorities are investigating. The complete original PDF was read. The source identity is marked verified by UKMTO, not independently verified by this review. Vessel identity, responsible actor, damage extent and exact publication time remain unknown. This newly reviewed notice concerns October 6, not a new October 8 or October 9 attack. JMIC Update 103 lists notices through 158-26 and supplies no independent corroboration of 159-26.
latest_news.originating_source: UKMTO original Warning 159-26
latest_news.implication: The notice adds a delayed report of an October 6 Hormuz transit strike, not a new attack today; damage and responsibility remain unknown.
latest_news.next_trigger: UKMTO says authorities are investigating; no findings date is supplied.

latest_news.headline: Newly reviewed UKMTO 158-26: October 7 tanker attack off Qatar; JMIC reports one injured
latest_news.text: The original UKMTO warning 158-26 dates the incident to October 7 at 19:00 UTC, 51 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar, and reports multiple projectile hits and unspecified casualties. JMIC Update 103, with an October 8 15:00 UTC information cutoff rather than a known publication instant, attributes a later account to the company security officer: three UAV hits, an engine-room fire subsequently extinguished, one crew member injured and the vessel able to continue. JMIC withholds the vessel's name; BBC's Vanguard-based vessel identification is not admitted as verified identity. Both primary documents were downloaded and read. No attack responsibility or independent physical confirmation is established. This newly reviewed report concerns October 7, not a new October 8 attack.
latest_news.originating_source: UKMTO original warning 158-26; JMIC original Update 103
latest_news.implication: The primary notice establishes a reported attack deeper in the Gulf; the later account reports one injury and continued voyage, not confirmed fatalities.
latest_news.next_trigger: UKMTO says authorities are investigating; no findings date is supplied.

latest_news.headline: UKMTO 153-26 correction: JMIC identifies LNG, not LPG, carrier and reports no crew injuries
latest_news.text: JMIC Update 103 identifies UKMTO 153-26 as an LNG carrier, contrary to the retained LPG label, and describes an October 4 inbound Hormuz strike by a suspected UAV. It reports no crew injuries and says the vessel continued its voyage. The retained original warning and its prior LPG description remain preserved; this is an explicit vessel-type correction and outcome revision of the same numbered notice. Exact publication instant, vessel identity and physical verification remain unknown.
latest_news.originating_source: Joint Maritime Information Center original Update 103
latest_news.implication: The retained vessel-type label is corrected to LNG; reported safe continuation does not establish regional de-escalation.
latest_news.next_trigger: No dated follow-up or independently evidenced next trigger is supplied by the reviewed product.
latest_news.material_revision: UKMTO 153-26 correction: JMIC identifies LNG, not LPG, carrier and reports no crew injuries

latest_news.headline: UKMTO 154-26 revision: JMIC reports two projectile hits and no crew injuries
latest_news.text: JMIC Update 103 links UKMTO 154-26 to an October 4 inbound Hormuz tanker strike near the Musandam peninsula, with two unknown projectiles and no crew injuries reported. This adds an attributed injury-status account to the retained incident without replacing the original notice. Vessel identity, damage extent, responsibility and independent physical verification remain unknown.
latest_news.originating_source: Joint Maritime Information Center original Update 103
latest_news.implication: The same tanker report now includes two projectile hits and an attributed no-injury account; damage and responsibility remain unknown.
latest_news.next_trigger: No dated follow-up or independently evidenced next trigger is supplied by the reviewed product.
latest_news.material_revision: UKMTO 154-26 revision: JMIC reports two projectile hits and no crew injuries

latest_news.headline: UKMTO 156-26 revision: JMIC reports LNG carrier fire extinguished and voyage continued
latest_news.text: JMIC Update 103 identifies UKMTO 156-26 as an LNG carrier and relays its master's October 5 outbound Hormuz projectile-strike account. It says the engine-room fire was extinguished, no crew injuries were reported and the vessel continued its voyage. This revises the retained report's unresolved fire and crew outcomes; the original report remains retained. Responsibility, damage extent and independent verification remain unknown.
latest_news.originating_source: Joint Maritime Information Center original Update 103
latest_news.implication: The same incident has an attributed extinguished-fire and continued-voyage outcome; this does not establish reduced transit risk.
latest_news.next_trigger: No dated follow-up or independently evidenced next trigger is supplied by the reviewed product.
latest_news.material_revision: UKMTO 156-26 revision: JMIC reports LNG carrier fire extinguished and voyage continued
